name: geo-api-mini-20
notes: 20-task geo mini: 8 definitions + 12 theorems. Always inject points/vec/dot/det so the model knows this is the analytic-geometry library. Some tasks also inject distance_sq.

tasks.name: distance_sq
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. The following are already defined and must not be redefined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define `distance_sq(a, b)` as the squared Euclidean distance between points a and b in cart(R, R), using vec and dot.
Output only the Litex definition.
tasks.gold: have fn distance_sq(a, b cart(R, R)) R = dot(vec(a, b), vec(a, b))

tasks.name: line
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define `line(a, b, c)` as the set of points p satisfying a*p(1)+b*p(2)+c=0, with domain guard `a != 0 or b != 0`.
Output only the Litex definition.
tasks.gold: have fn line(a, b, c R: a != 0 or b != 0) power_set(cart(R, R)) = {p cart(R, R): a * p(1) + b * p(2) + c = 0}

tasks.name: line_through_points
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define `line_through_points(a, b)` for a != b as the set of points p collinear with a,b via det(vec(a,p), vec(a,b)) = 0.
Output only the Litex definition.
tasks.gold: have fn line_through_points(a, b cart(R, R): a != b) power_set(cart(R, R)) = {p cart(R, R): det(vec(a, p), vec(a, b)) = 0}

tasks.name: angle_cos_num
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define `angle_cos_num(p, q, r)` (with p!=q and r!=q) as the numerator of the cosine of angle at q: dot(vec(q,p), vec(q,r)).
Output only the Litex definition.
tasks.gold: have fn angle_cos_num(p, q, r cart(R, R): p != q, r != q) R = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))

tasks.name: circle
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det, distance_sq.
Define `circle(o, r)` for r in R+ as the set of points p with distance_sq(o, p) = r * r.
Output only the Litex definition.
tasks.gold: have fn circle(o cart(R, R), r R+) power_set(cart(R, R)) = {p cart(R, R): distance_sq(o, p) = r * r}

tasks.name: is_on_segment
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define prop `is_on_segment(p, a, b)`: a != b and there exists t in [0,1] with p the affine combination of a and b.
Output only the Litex prop.

tasks.name: is_collinear
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Define prop `is_collinear(p, q, r)` as det(vec(p, q), vec(p, r)) = 0.
Output only the Litex prop.
tasks.gold:
prop is_collinear(p, q, r cart(R, R)):
    det(vec(p, q), vec(p, r)) = 0

tasks.name: are_segments_congruent
tasks.prompt_en:
You are extending a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det, distance_sq.
Define prop `are_segments_congruent(a, b, c, d)` as equal squared lengths.
Output only the Litex prop.
tasks.gold:
prop are_segments_congruent(a, b, c, d cart(R, R)):
    distance_sq(a, b) = distance_sq(c, d)

tasks.name: vec_coordinate_formula
tasks.statement:
thm vec_coordinate_formula:
    ? forall a, b cart(R, R):
        vec(a, b) = (b(1) - a(1), b(2) - a(2))
tasks.prompt_en:
You are proving theorems in a planar analytic-geometry library. Already defined: points, vec, dot, det.
Prove the following theorem. Keep the statement unchanged. You may leave an empty proof body if the checker accepts unfolding.

thm vec_coordinate_formula:
    ? forall a, b cart(R, R):
        vec(a, b) = (b(1) - a(1), b(2) - a(2))

tasks.name: dot_coordinate_formula
tasks.statement:
thm dot_coordinate_formula:
    ? forall u, v cart(R, R):
        dot(u, v) = u(1) * v(1) + u(2) * v(2)
tasks.prompt_en:

tasks.name: collinear_det_expand
tasks.statement:
thm collinear_det_expand:
    ? forall p, q, r cart(R, R):
        det(vec(p, q), vec(p, r)) = (q(1) - p(1)) * (r(2) - p(2)) - (q(2) - p(2)) * (r(1) - p(1))
tasks.prompt_en:
Library already has points, vec, dot, det. Prove with the statement unchanged:

        det(vec(p, q), vec(p, r)) = (q(1) - p(1)) * (r(2) - p(2)) - (q(2) - p(2)) * (r(1) - p(1))
